The biological and cultural permits include the water quality review. This review deals with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permits to sources of wastewater discharge into streams, lakes, and other water bodies. Since wastewater discharge is a standard procedure in chemical industries/ projects, it is mandatory to acquire permits and authorizations regarding the various aspects of wastewater discharge. These permits include a water discharge permit for construction, a new/modified drainage permit, a wastewater treatment permit, and a wastewater permit. The waste permit consists of the permit for a Class VI well for the sequestration of CO . This is the most sensitive and critical permit for the envisaged project and has the 2 highest estimated review/ approval time. The permit would test the suitability of Class VI wells and validate the safety of CO sequestration in the proposed well. The state of Indiana requires other permits and 2 authorizations. Such permits include final building permits, temporary building & construction permits, and tall structure construction permits. These permits validate the building construction and ensure that the buildings are within the permissible heights approved by the concerned agency. 3.0 Broad List of Permits Needed This note broadly mentions the permits needed for setting up a Carbon Capture (CC) facility in the existing Burn Harbor Plant of Cliffs.
